is_edible removed on audit: This fails the edibility safety check (F), and the unknowns misstate the pages. The unknowns claim 'Neither page carries a prose toxicity paragraph.' That is false. Clemson HGIC says in prose: 'The sticky white sap may irritate skin or the stomach if eaten. Keep these plants away from any pets or young children that tend to eat plants.' The researcher's own rule-5 search list included 'Toxic' but evidently not 'irritat' or 'sap', so it missed this. The toxic part (the sap) and the ingestion warning never appear in unknowns. The only toxicity note there is NC State's '#problem for dogs/horses/cats' tags, which cover pets only and name no part. Beyond that, 'true' rests on a weak basis: NC State calls the fruit only 'barely edible' and says 'Fruiting is rare when grown indoors.' For a houseplant whose one toxicity statement warns against eating it, is_edible=true with the sap irritant left out cannot stand. Null it.
